# Citation

Wick, R. R., et al. (2017). *Unicycler: resolving bacterial genome assemblies from short and long sequencing reads*. PLoS Computational Biology. DOI: 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005595. Source: [https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005595](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005595).

# One-Sentence Summary

Presents Unicycler, a bacterial hybrid assembler that integrates short-read assembly graphs with long reads to improve contiguity and resolve repeats.

# Scope for simitall

Use as the intended hybrid-assembly backend in the bacterial benchmark pipeline. Keep raw read generation, assembly execution, and reference-based evaluation as separate recorded stages.

# Agent-Safe Takeaways

- Short reads provide base accuracy while long reads help resolve graph ambiguity and repeats.
- Hybrid assembly performance depends on both read sets, not only long-read depth.
- Assembly results should be compared with a known truth reference using transparent QC metrics.

# Inputs to Specify

- Paired short reads
- Long reads
- Output directory, threads, and assembly mode

# Expected Outputs

- Assembly FASTA
- Assembly graph and logs
- Tool-specific diagnostics

# Limitations and Guardrails

- Designed for bacterial genomes and not a general eukaryotic assembly solution.
- Contiguity alone is not evidence of correctness; use reference-aware quality assessment for simulations.

# Questions This Record Can Ground

- Why run a coverage grid for hybrid assembly?
- Which output files from Unicycler should be retained for debugging and evaluation?
